name: Early evolutionary and scientific speculation of Anaximander
plain_explanation: Anaximander held that the world was not created but evolved out of eternal motion, that living creatures arose from moisture evaporated by the sun, and that humans must have descended from a different kind of animal, since a human infant's long helplessness would not have allowed the species to survive if it had always been as it is now.
precise_definition: Anaximander's naturalistic account of cosmic and biological origins, including the claim that man is descended from fish-like ancestors, and his practical scientific work including the first map and various (differing) estimates of the sun's size relative to the earth.
why_it_mattered: Shows Russell's view of the Milesians as genuinely scientific and rationalistic 'wherever they are original', prefiguring, however crudely, the mechanistic and non-mythological cast of later Ionian and atomist thought.
historical_origin: Attributed to Anaximander by later sources including Aristotle and doxographers.
examples: The first known map, attributed to Anaximander
Varying ancient estimates that the sun is as large as the earth, or 27 or 28 times as large
competing_positions: Anaximenes' and the later atomists' view that the earth is disc- or table-shaped, as opposed to the (later) Pythagorean discovery that the earth is spherical

evolution.treatment: Anaximander held that the world was not created but evolved out of eternal motion, that living creatures arose from moisture evaporated by the sun, and that humans must have descended from a different kind of animal, since a human infant's long helplessness would not have allowed the species to survive if it had always been as it is now.
